DATED: 16/04/2024  unde  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE  FIR/ORDER) NO. 1923 of 2024 ==========================================================
 NARESHBHAI KANJIBHAI CHAMRIYA (PATEL) & ORS.
 Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
==========================================================
Appearance:
KULDEEP J MEHTA(8571) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3 MR ABHAYKUMAR P SHAH(3093) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3 MAHESH PUJARA, for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MS CM SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE HASMUKH D. SUTHAR  Date : 16/04/2024

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.
Learned advocate Mr. Mahesh Pujara states that he has instructions to appear on behalf of the original complainant and thereby, seeks permission to file his Vakalatnama, which is granted.
2. RULE.
Learned advocates waive service of note of rule on behalf of the respective respondents.

3. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and since it is jointly stated at the bar by learned advocates on both the sides that the dispute between the parties has been resolved amicably,
this matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

4. By way of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "Cr.P.C."), the applicants have prayed to quash and set aside the complaint being FIR No.11993003231251 of 2023 registered with Anjar Police Station, Dist. Kachchh, for the offences under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120 B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all the Nareshbhai Kanjibhai Chamriya (Patel) vs State Of Gujarat on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148731067/
1 consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

undefined 5.

Learned advocates for the respective parties submitted that during the pendency of proceedings,
the parties have settled the dispute amicably and pursuant to such mutual settlement, the original complainant has also filed an Affidavit, which is taken / placed on record.

In the Affidavit, the original complainant has categorically stated that the dispute with the applicant/s has been resolved amicably and that he has no objection, if the present proceedings are quashed and set aside since there is no surviving grievance between them.

6. Having heard learned advocates on both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case as also the principle laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of (I) Kunti & Anr. Vs. State of U.P & Anr. reported in (2023) 6 SCC 109, (ii) Sarabjit Kaur Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. Reported in (2023) 5 SCC 360, (iii) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, (iv)
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, (v) Nikhil Merchant Vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 31, (vi) Manoj Sharma Vs. State &
Ors., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 190, (vii) Rekha Jain Vs. State of Karnataka, reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 468, and (viii) Narinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported in 2014 (2)
Crime 67 (SC), in the opinion of this Court, the further continuation of criminal proceedings, more particularly offence under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC against the applicant/s in relation to the impugned FIR would cause unnecessary harassment to the applicant/s.
